headline: Models learn cell identity and tissue structure from single-cell and spatial omics
label: Machine Learning For Spatial Omics
summary: Recent preprints apply transformers and graph models to H&E-based expression prediction, spatial domain identification, and clustering evaluation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations that link single-cell and spatial transcriptomic or imaging data to cell identity and tissue organization. COAST predicts spatial gene expression from H&E images with a Transformer over spot tokens, while BertST applies a BERT transformer to spatial domain identification using random-walk node embeddings over multi-graphs. CSGDA uses graph domain adaptation for single-cell drug response across platforms, and HASSL combines segmentation-teacher distillation with HDBSCAN-based contrastive learning for single-cell microscopy. Syto extends soft-labeled deconvolution to read-level DNA methylation over a 39-cell-type atlas. Distinct contributions include evaluation infrastructure: MultimetricST combines label-dependent and label-independent metrics for spatial domain clustering, and InfoDPP-PAC applies diversity-aware patch selection to whole slide images. Published graph-based multi-view models, including IDEAL and HDBI, address microbe-drug and ncRNA-drug association prediction, a related but distinct application.
